title: Deep Vessel Segmentation Based on a New Combination of Vesselness Filters
mechanism: Train the segmentation net on stacked multi-scale vesselness filter responses instead of (or with) the raw image; helps small vessels.
adaptation: Add Frangi / Sato / Jerman responses for dark ridges at sigma 1, 1.5, 2, 3 px as extra input channels to house U-Net++ (no training of the filters). Fingers and busbar edges will respond too.
min_experiment: Arm: house with [EL, 4 ridge maps], 5 seeds; baseline house 5 seeds. Metrics: crack relF1@2, E1 relF1@2, gridline IoU. Kill: crack and E1 relF1@2 gains both < 0.01. Note HarmonySeg found plain concatenation gave no notable gain, so a null here then points to attention fusion.
evidence: U-Net on vesselness hyper-volumes improved segmentation, mainly small vessels, on two vascular datasets (abstract). HarmonySeg ablation: simple CT+vesselness concatenation gave no notable gain.

alt_notes.adaptation: Input stack: raw, Sato dark-ridge sigma 1 and 2, Frangi dark-ridge, FFT residual. Use 4 to 5 channels, with the conv1 extra-channel weights zero-initialised.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house with the 4-channel stack, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: test relF1@2, E1 crack recall. Kill: E1 recall < +0.03 and relF1@2 < +0.01.
